Companies House Email Scam UK: Spot a Fake Notice

Real Companies House email addresses end in `.gov.uk`, but verify requests through GOV.UK rather than trusting the sender name or a link.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-04-27 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 2 min read

Companies House email scamfake Companies House emailCompanies House phishing UKCompanies House impersonation scamUK business email scamemail scam UKphishing email UK
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.

What the scam looks like

Fraudsters impersonate Companies House in emails about overdue filings, payments, WebFiling, identity verification or removal from the register. The message may use a lookalike domain, urgent deadline, attachment or link to collect credentials, personal codes or payment information.

Current identity-verification context

Identity verification became a legal requirement from 18 November 2025, but that date began a phased transition rather than creating one deadline for every existing director and person with significant control. New directors generally need to verify for appointment or incorporation; existing directors usually provide their personal code with the company’s next confirmation statement, and PSC timing depends on their role and due date.

Scammers can exploit this real process. Do not assume an identity-verification message is genuine merely because the requirement exists.

Warning signs

  • The sender address does not end in .gov.uk exactly.
  • Pressure to pay, open an attachment or act immediately.
  • A link destination that differs from the expected GOV.UK or Companies House address.
  • A request for a password, bank details, authentication code or other secure information.
  • A demand to verify through a site reached only from the email.

Companies House says it will not call to ask for passwords, bank details, authentication codes or director/officer details. Its scam guidance also lists known fraudulent domains and current examples.

Verify independently

Open GOV.UK yourself and use the Companies House service to check filings, company status and identity-verification due dates. Do not use the message’s link, attachment or callback number.

An email ending in .gov.uk is an important check, but no sender-domain test is infallible. Treat the requested action and destination as separate things to verify.

If you entered information

Change affected passwords from a clean device, remove unfamiliar sessions, and contact the bank immediately if card or account information was entered. If an authentication or personal code was exposed, contact Companies House through GOV.UK for current security steps.

Reporting

Forward a suspicious Companies House email to phishing@companieshouse.gov.uk. If money was lost, report at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101.

Frequently asked questions

Did every existing director have to verify by 18 November 2025?

No. That date started mandatory requirements and a phased transition. Check the due date for the particular role through GOV.UK.

Will Companies House ask for my authentication code by email or phone?

Its published scam guidance says it will never call asking for an authentication code or other secure information. Do not disclose the code in response to an unsolicited email either; verify through the official service.

Where should a suspicious email be sent?

phishing@companieshouse.gov.uk.
